name: Minimum size of maximum regular induced subgraph of a graph on n vertices.
comment: This is similar to Ramsey numbers, except we consider not only complete and independent subgraphs but any regular induced subgraph.
link: Paul W. Dyson and Brendan D. McKay, Ramsey numbers for regular induced subgraphs, arXiv:2604.08215 [math.CO] (2026).
Paul Dyson and Brendan McKay, Ramsey Graphs (section Regular induced subgraphs)
Erdős problems database contributors, Computations of F(n) and t(n) from #82.
S. Fajtlowicz, T. McColgan, T. Reid, and W. Staton, Ramsey numbers for induced regular subgraphs, Ars Combinatoria, 39 (1995) 149-154.
formula: a(n) = max{ k | A394563(k) <= n }. - _Brendan McKay_, Apr 11 2026
example: Every graph on 5 vertices either contains the complete graph on 3 vertices or its complement, or the graph is the 5-cycle which is itself regular. Moreover, the tree {13,23,34,45} has no regular induced subgraph greater than 3. So a(5)=3.
author: _Boris Alexeev_, Oct 30 2025
